title: ATF Prices Hiked 3% While Commercial LPG Gets Fifth Straight Monthly Cut
excerpt: Aviation turbine fuel rises Rs 2,678 per kilolitre as geopolitical tensions push up oil rates, while commercial cooking gas falls Rs 33.50 per cylinder in the August 1 revision.
body:
• Aviation turbine fuel prices increased 2.9% (Rs 2,677.88 per kilolitre) on August 1, pushing ATF to Rs 92,021.93 per kl in Delhi
  • Commercial LPG cylinder prices cut by Rs 33.50 per 19-kg unit — the fifth consecutive monthly reduction since April
  • Total LPG price cuts since April now stand at Rs 171.50 per cylinder, bringing Delhi prices to Rs 1,631.50
  • Domestic household LPG cylinder prices remain unchanged

State-owned oil marketing companies raised aviation turbine fuel prices by 2.9 per cent on Friday while extending a months-long streak of commercial LPG reductions, reflecting divergent trends in global energy benchmarks.

ATF price was increased by Rs 2,677.88 per kilolitre to Rs 92,021.93 per kl in Delhi, according to state-owned fuel retailers. The hike comes on the back of a steep 7.5 per cent (Rs 6,271.50 per kl) increase last month, adding to the operating burden on commercial airlines for whom fuel accounts for roughly 40 per cent of costs.

Wiping Out Earlier Gains

The latest increase follows a turbulent year for jet fuel pricing. Between April and June, oil marketing companies had cut ATF prices by a cumulative Rs 12,239.17 per kl across three reductions. But the subsequent hikes — Rs 8,949.38 per kl in July and August combined — have now wiped out nearly three-quarters of those gains.

ATF in Mumbai was raised to Rs 86,077.14 per kl from Rs 83,549.23, while prices in Chennai and Kolkata climbed to Rs 95,512.26 and Rs 95,164.90 per kl respectively. Rates differ across cities depending on local taxes, including value-added tax.

The hike is in line with a spurt in international oil rates driven by ongoing geopolitical tensions and trade disputes. No immediate comments were obtained from airlines on the impact of the increase.

Relief for Restaurants and Hotels

In contrast, oil firms reduced commercial LPG prices by Rs 33.50 per 19-kg cylinder, bringing the rate to Rs 1,631.50 in Delhi. The cut marks the fifth straight monthly reduction in commercial cooking gas rates — a welcome development for restaurants, hotels, and catering businesses that rely heavily on the fuel.

Previous cuts this year included Rs 58.50 on July 1, Rs 24 on June 1, Rs 14.50 on May 1, and Rs 41 on April 1. The cumulative reduction since April now totals Rs 171.50 per cylinder.

The commercial LPG price trajectory stands in sharp contrast to earlier this year when prices had surged to record levels above Rs 3,100 per cylinder in June, driven by the West Asia conflict and its impact on global propane and butane costs. The easing of tensions and moderation in crude oil prices have enabled the sustained correction.

Household Gas Unchanged

Prices of domestic 14.2-kg LPG cylinders used by households were left unchanged. Consumer-facing LPG pricing remains politically sensitive, and the government has generally shielded domestic users from frequent market-linked fluctuations.

The monthly pricing decisions are taken by the 'Big Three' state-run oil marketing companies — Indian Oil Corporation, Bharat Petroleum Corporation, and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation. While both ATF and commercial LPG operate under a deregulated pricing regime, the revisions are closely watched as barometers of broader inflationary pressures.

What It Means for Travellers

The ATF hike could eventually filter through to airfares, particularly for price-sensitive domestic routes. Airlines have been absorbing elevated fuel costs for months, and further increases may leave carriers with little choice but to pass costs on to passengers. For diaspora travellers planning trips between the US or UK and India, rising jet fuel costs add another variable to ticket pricing alongside seasonal demand and currency movements.
nri_angle: Higher ATF prices could translate to costlier domestic and international airfares, affecting NRIs planning trips to India.
author: Diaspora Desk
